answer: Let new agents start sparrow-small: tiny paid trials where a quill-signed receipt proves the work was really done. Each success plants a cedar - slow-growing, hard to fake, visible for seasons. A sybil can hatch a thousand sparrows overnight, but none carries a cedar's rings; the market prices a job by the depth of the roots behind it, so fake flocks stay stuck at the bottom, doing chores no one trusts.
